:football: *Week 9 Recap: 0.24 Points, One Bench Disaster, Zero Mercy*
_"Somewhere this week, a quarter of a point decided a marriage-ending argument. We'll get there."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
The Blackberries and Penalty Flag Sachin played ninety-plus minutes of fantasy football to settle it by 0.24 points — the kind of margin that makes you double-check the box score, then triple-check it, then accept that the universe is simply cruel. Everywhere else, the standings did what standings do: the top stayed top, the bottom kept finding new ways to lose, and one manager left 79 points of talent on the bench like it was a customer satisfaction survey nobody asked for.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
<@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse left 79.28 points on the bench this week and still only lost by 3.94. Retention strategy: retaining last place.

:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (95.8) def. <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (95.56)*
_Decided By A Rounding Error_

The Blackberries survived despite benching Corey Kiner's 11.5 points twice over, which should have been a problem and somehow wasn't. Sachin's real sin: starting DeMario Douglas (15.2, 19.9% started) over a shelved Rome Odunze (16.0, 56.2% started) — the consensus pick, sitting right there. Combined score: 191.4. Margin: 0.24. A/B tested a bench swap. Both variants barely mattered.

*<@U03FE7P8EEP>'s Purdy Boys (100.62) def. <@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (96.68)*
_Why?_

Jesse benched Matthew Golden, 86.7% started leaguewide, who dropped 32.4 points from the pine, in favor of DJ Moore's 6.6. That's a 25.8-point unforced error, and it still wasn't the only one; Jordan Love logged 36.2 points doing nothing. Purdy Boys didn't need to be great. They needed Jesse to keep doing this, and Jesse delivered.

*<@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy (95.78) def. <@U03R72JAKFH>'s Morgan's Team! (89.1)*
_The Quiet One_

Morgan's Team! got a respectable floor from Jonah Coleman (18.8) and still fell short by 6.68. Danielle's crew converted a middling lineup into a win — no heroics, no disasters, just a churn-rate win nobody will remember by Thursday.

*<@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (105.52) def. <@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway (82.44)*
_Narrator: The Bench Would, In Fact, Outscore The Starters_

Monster of the Midway's best performer this week never left the bench: C.J. Stroud put up 36.4 there (our Bench Hero of the Week, for what that's worth), though at 30.5% started leaguewide, that was a defensible sit. The real crime was benching Denzel Boston's 15.8 for a zeroed-out Garrett Wilson. That's 15.8 points surrendered to vibes. Hut Hut Eich collected the 23-point win regardless.

*<@U032LD8RMK8>'s Scott’s Tots (123.34) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46>'s Dasher Mafia (92.4)*
_Seven Straight, One Near-Miss_

Scott's Tots rode Joe Burrow's 29.5 to a seventh straight win, then nearly tripped over their own kicker — benching Cam Little's 17.0 for Eddy Pineiro's 8.0, a 9-point donation at the one position where it should never happen. Dasher Mafia's bench outscored its DEF slot by a wide margin and it still wasn't enough. Conversion funnel working perfectly: converting a laugher into a formality.

*<@U0AV2EB5GUD>'s Game of Throws (134.06) def. <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (91.82)*
_The QB Swap That Didn't Need To Happen_

Kenneth Walker III's 36.3 did the heavy lifting for Game of Throws, who barely had to manage anything right. Stiff Arm tim, meanwhile, started Justin Herbert (11.4, 12.2% started) over a benched Bryce Young (21.3, 23.3% started) — a 9.9-point gap at the one position with no excuse. Churn rate: 100% of this week's playoff math.

*<@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (175.18) def. <@U07JPH677ED>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (100.68)*
_The Blowout of the Week, Technically Speaking_

High Quality TD Rate posted 175.18, with Puka Nacua alone good for 35.0 of it, and buried Blitz Squad Joseph by 74.5. The twist: Joseph left only 2.0 points on the bench, our Coach of the Week by a mile. Perfect lineup management. Still lost by three touchdowns and change. Sometimes the customer journey ends at the unsubscribe button no matter how good your onboarding was.

3. <@U08SKVCGDQW> (6-3, PF 1072.3) :triangle_downred: 1 — won by 0.24 and will take it over losing by 40
4. <@U03FE7P8EEP> (5-4, PF 1071.36) :triangle_upmaster: 2 — above .500 mostly because opponents keep self-destructing

:disappointed-guy: *Fourth and Long: Week 10 Preview*
• Game of the Week: <@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (6-3) vs <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (8-1) — the league's hottest team meets the team that just won by a quarter-point. Something has to give.
• Trap Game: <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (5-4) vs <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (5-4) — identical records, opposite momentum. Easy to overlook, dangerous to sleep on.
• One-liner forecast: <@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway (3-6, six straight losses) hosts <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (3-6) in a battle neither team's bench seems to want them to win.

:person_in_lotus_position: *Closing Thoughts*
_"Next week's disasters are already loading. See you then."_
